title: Recurring unresolved limitation 'study-heterogeneity' across 3 independent papers
explanation: 3 independent papers (2015–2022) report an own-work limitation normalized to 'study-heterogeneity'. Mixed-fidelity: 2 full-text, 1 abstract-only; score corrected for the ~11x full-text detection bias = 0.687 vs uncorrected 0.618. Methodological diversity: 4 distinct methods (NOTE: diversity/time-span weighting extends beyond opportunity-criteria.md). Resolution is ASSUMED absent — no limitation-resolution relation exists in Phase 3, so 'unresolved' is unverified. Example limitation statements: The included articles vary significantly in study design (ranging from systematic reviews to clinical studies, | Quantitative meta-analysis pooling of results was not possible due to heterogeneity in study objectives and ou | Wide heterogeneity in design, sample size, measurement instruments, and results across included studies temper. Papers: openalex:W1892688171; openalex:W2593771132; openalex:W4291885054.

caveats.label: Mixed-fidelity
caveats.detail: 1 supporting paper(s) are abstract-only, which yield ~11x fewer own-work limitations than full text.

The included articles vary significantly in study design (ranging from systematic reviews to clinical studies, letters, and editorials), making accurate comparison difficult.
Quantitative meta-analysis pooling of results was not possible due to heterogeneity in study objectives and outcomes.
Wide heterogeneity in design, sample size, measurement instruments, and results across included studies tempers any firm conclusions.

consumer.headline: 3 separate teams ran into the same wall: study heterogeneity
consumer.kind_short: A problem that several independent teams ran into
consumer.kind_long: Papers describe the limits of their own work. When separate teams — who did not build on each other — keep reporting the same limit, that is a sign of a real obstacle rather than one group's bad luck.
consumer.strength_meaning: There is real evidence behind this, but it rests on a small number of papers — read them before trusting it.
consumer.why: 3 separate research teams each reported hitting this in their own work. They did not build on each other, so this is unlikely to be one group's bad luck. Their papers span 1 years. We could read 2 of them in full, which is where teams describe what actually went wrong.

caveats.label: Based partly on summaries only
caveats.text: For some of these papers we only had the summary, not the full text. Papers we could read in full reveal far more about their own limits, so this may be built on an incomplete picture.
